bullets.title: META: Mixed reaction to Q3 beat — Muse momentum vs. capex overhang driving -5-6% stock
bullets.body: META Q3 revenue $64.60B (+26.1% YoY) beat $63.34B consensus; U.S./Canada ad revenue +33.3% YoY (3rd consecutive acceleration); Q4 guide $73-76B midpoint +24.4% vs. +23.0% consensus. However, stock down 5-6% as full-year capex narrowed to $135-145B (87-101% YoY growth), 2027 capex deferred to Q4 call, FCF turned negative at -$2.12B, and CDS spread hit all-time high of 114.5bps. Muse has 10M+ users in 1.5 months with 25% DAU rate and $200+ avg purchase; Class C stock issuance announced for Jan 2027 capital raise. Bull case: Mizuho raises PT to $950 (from $750), Citi raises to $905; Bear case: Oppenheimer sidelined citing $30-50B equity overhang and below-Street 2028 EPS of $36.25.

bullets.title: SPOT: +8% premarket on Q3 premium subs beat; Q4 GM guide 33.8% above Street
bullets.body: Spotify Q3 revenue €4.97B (+14% YoY), premium subs +6M exceeded guidance of +5M, and FCF €735M. Q4 guidance: revenue €5.2B (slightly below Street), operating income €820M (above Street), gross margin 33.8% (above MS est. of 33.5%). Ad revenue tracking toward double-digit growth in H2; AI investments cited for better discovery and engagement. Key uncertainty: timing of marketing, AI, and cloud spend normalization.

bullets.title: CMCSA: Q3 beat on EBITDA/EPS/FCF but broadband -144k net adds and theme parks weaken
bullets.body: Comcast Q3 revenue $29.3B beat consensus ($29.2B); EPS $1.07 beat $0.97 consensus; FCF $4.2B beat $3.4B consensus. Broadband net losses -144k slightly wider than expected though ARPU decline of -2.9% was better than -3.3% consensus. Theme parks revenue below consensus with Orlando softness expected through H1 2027. NBCUniversal/Sky separation tracking for mid-2027; $1B+ transformation charge expected in Q4. Citi maintains Buy at $27.50 PT.

bullets.title: MU: Citi Buy maintained; $35B buyback, 3D DRAM roadmap, AI memory demand in focus
bullets.body: Citi hosted Micron CFO investor meetings and reiterates Buy. Key themes: $35B share repurchase program (largest in company history), 3D DRAM technology roadmap (not pursuing 4F2 due to complexity/cost), and AI-driven memory demand growth. Hedgeye flagged MU as a long signal after Taichung union labor agreement reduced production interruption risk. DA Davidson reiterates Buy with $3,000 PT citing leadership position in AI memory with wider moats than valuation implies.

bullets.title: TSLA: FSD attach >75% (+20ppt q/q), Robotaxi miles +30% w/w; MS raises PT to $410
bullets.body: Tesla North American FSD attach rates exceeded 75% (up 20ppt q/q) with paid FSD customers >1.7M. Robotaxi autonomous miles ~558k/week with 30% week-over-week growth; Cybercab deployment up 10x with four new city launches. Energy storage demand robust and automotive margins improving, though OpEx scaling faster than expected. Morgan Stanley raises PT to $410 from $400; SPCX advisers reportedly pushing for TSLA merger announcement by 1H27.

bullets.title: LRCX: -10.1% premarket on earnings; AMAT/KLAC down ~6% in sympathy
bullets.body: Lam Research down 10.1% premarket on earnings. AMAT and KLAC fell ~6.2% in sympathy. One analyst argues the inline guide is supply-chain driven, not demand peak — 2027 WFE growing >29% YoY with DRAM/logic/NAND tailwinds, and sentiment is overselling 2028 peak fears. Wolfresearch hosting semiconductor earnings preview webcast covering LRCX and TXN.

bullets.title: TXN: Big beat and raise — Q3 revenue $6.06B vs $5.92B cons; Q4 EPS guide $2.62 vs $2.30 cons
bullets.body: Texas Instruments beat Q3 gross margin at 64.2% vs. estimated 61.2%; Q3 revenue $6.06B vs. $5.92B consensus; Q4 EPS guidance $2.62 vs. $2.30 consensus. AI data center growing near 100% YoY described as GM accretive. Prior GM peak was 69-70% at $4.9-5.2B quarterly revenue, suggesting consensus 2027-28 estimates of flat GMs are too conservative. Stock initially weak despite beat, seen as eventual buy on AI fear normalization.

bullets.title: NVDA: 2027 demand growth near +100% vs +70% guided; GTC supply chain update
bullets.body: NVDA 2027 demand growth tracking near +100% vs. +70% revenue guidance; supply-chain capacity expanding but TSMC 3nm remains main bottleneck. CEO noted neocloud demand strong but capital scarce for expansion. Hedgeye carries a short signal on NVDA post-GTC Europe citing Meta 2026 capex not raised and Trump energy mandate cost headwinds. McCullough's macro framework now contains substantially more AI shorts than two weeks prior, with memory stocks flagged as second layer to break after neoclouds.

bullets.title: PLTR: Citi raises PT to $250 from $245 on expected double-digit beats in USG and Commercial
bullets.body: Citi raised Palantir PT to $250 from $245 ahead of Q3 earnings, citing expected double-digit percentage beats in U.S. Government and Commercial segments, with upside driven by deeper collaboration across technology stack including NeoClouds.

bullets.title: CLS/Celestica: Down 9.2% in Canada trading; no new fundamental catalyst cited
bullets.body: Celestica (CLS) fell 9.2% to C$389.01 on the Toronto Stock Exchange mid-morning, among the largest decliners in a broad market selloff. No company-specific news catalyst was identified. JPMorgan has a post-earnings analyst webcast with CLS scheduled for October 28.

bullets.title: IBM: Citi raises PT to $280 from $245; VMware displacement opportunity and Red Hat growth key
bullets.body: IBM Q3 headline revenue +6% YoY in constant currency beat Street by 3%, accelerating 5pts QoQ. Virtualization bookings ~$800M TCV with $750M pipeline; 2027 VMware renewal expiries create displacement opportunity. OpenShift now ~35% of subscription ARR growing >30%; HashiCorp bookings growing 20%. 4Q transaction processing implies -1% YoY on difficult comps. Citi maintains Buy at $280 PT.

bullets.title: GLW: Q3 earnings Oct 27; consensus $5.03B rev and $0.88 EPS; options pricing ~9.7% move
bullets.body: Corning reports Q3 on October 27. Consensus expects $5.03B revenue (vs. $4.9-5.0B guidance) and $0.88 EPS (vs. $0.85-0.89 guidance). Options market pricing ~9.7% post-earnings move. GLW has beaten revenue consensus 17 of past 20 quarters and EPS 15 of 20. JPMorgan has a post-earnings webcast scheduled for October 28.

bullets.title: AVGO: Tigress Financial initiates Buy with $600 PT, 78% upside from $337.80
bullets.body: Tigress Financial Partners initiated Broadcom with a Buy rating and $600 price target, representing 78% upside from $337.80. FactSet average target sits at $529.75 (range $350-$660). No specific fundamental catalyst cited in the initiation note.

bullets.title: NET: +2% premarket; NSA PHP vulnerability warning cited as cybersecurity tailwind
bullets.body: Cloudflare up 2.0% in premarket trading. Citi notes NSA PHP vulnerability warning is creating a cybersecurity tailwind benefiting NET and FSLY. Separately, an expert call is scheduled for Friday featuring a seven-figure NET and Akamai customer discussing agentic AI impact on CDN/security demand.

bullets.title: HUT: Down 7.5% in Canada trading; MS analyst overweight on crypto mining names
bullets.body: Hut 8 (HUT) fell 7.5% to C$92.97 in Toronto mid-morning in a broad sector selloff. Morgan Stanley's Powered Shells analyst maintains overweight ratings on HUT, WULF, RIOT, GLXY, and CIFR. Hedgeye's macro framework has been rotating away from the AI/tech framework toward cash and fixed income.

bullets.title: OKLO: At 52-week low of $27.00, down 80.7% over past year
bullets.body: Oklo (OKLO) hit a 52-week low at $27.00 (-2.8% on the session), down 80.7% over the past 52 weeks. No company-specific catalyst cited; the broader nuclear/energy sector is under pressure alongside AI infrastructure concerns.

bullets.title: MSFT/AMZN: Hedgeye adds MSFT long and moves AMZN to buy column
bullets.body: Hedgeye's Keith McCullough exited QQQ and rotated into a Microsoft-linked income ETF (MSFY), citing healthier signals. Amazon was moved into the buy column. Both names viewed as benefiting from AI cloud infrastructure buildout with less capex overhang risk than pure-play AI names. MSFT's $30B UK AI infrastructure investment flagged as facing community consent bottleneck.

bullets.title: NFLX: Q4 guide below Street on revenue and operating income; content reset underway
bullets.body: Netflix Q3 beat on content timing but Q4 revenue and operating income guide came in below Street expectations. Ad revenue tracking ~$2.7B vs ~$3B expected; management blamed slower rollout, not demand weakness. Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria replaced by Peter Rice, described as an execution reset. FY26 on track to finish below starting guidance for first time in three years.

bullets.title: SMCI: Raises Q1 2027 revenue guidance to $18.5-19.5B from $14.5-15.5B on AI platform demand
bullets.body: Supermicro raised Q1 2027 revenue guidance materially to $18.5-19.5B from $14.5-15.5B, citing strong AI platform demand. The guidance increase was highlighted across multiple sell-side summaries as a standout AI infrastructure data point distinct from hyperscaler capex concerns.

bullets.title: RBLX: RJ Market Perform ahead of Oct 29 earnings; Steal an Egg viral engagement peaking
bullets.body: Raymond James reiterates Market Perform on Roblox ahead of October 29 earnings. Steal an Egg viral game showing signs of peaking and redistributing existing engagement rather than attracting net new users. Mobile MAUs up double-digits YoY but platform concurrent users down double-digits YoY. RJ sees downside risk to Q4 bookings guidance on difficult comparisons.
